lesson.subtitle: Lesson 23 -- Culture: Brazilian vs American Business (Superlatives, As ... As)
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rafael Gasparelli Lima | Lesson 23 -- Two Business Cultures
lesson.grammar_point: superlatives with the most / the least and best / worst + (not) as ... as for comparing cultures

listenings.text: Doing business in the United States is not as slow as in many other countries. For most American managers, time is the most important thing. Meetings usually start on the minute, so you should be punctual. Small talk is short: maybe two minutes about the weekend or the weather, and then people go straight to business. Americans are usually very direct. If they don't like your offer, they say it clearly, and it is not rude. The hierarchy is not as strong as in Brazil, so a junior manager can disagree with a director in a meeting. People use first names from day one, and the dress code is often casual. But one thing is the same everywhere: the best deals come from a good relationship.

Hi, I'm Mark, and I buy fruit for a company in Chicago. My first trip to Brazil was a big surprise. The meeting in São Paulo started thirty minutes late, and nobody was worried. Before we talked about prices, we had a long lunch, and my Brazilian partners asked about my family. At first I thought it was a waste of time. Now I think that lunch was the most useful hour of the trip. In Brazil, the relationship comes first, and the contract comes later. My advice? Be patient, be polite, and learn a few words in Portuguese. The warmest welcome I ever had was in Brazil, and it was the best deal of my year.

extra_audio.text: First, Claire arrives in São Paulo for her first visit to Picunha. Then, Rafael welcomes her with some small talk about her trip. Next, they have a long lunch and talk about their families. After that, they discuss the contract in the meeting room. Finally, they agree that the relationship is the most important part of the deal.
